label: Dismissive responses and gestures
summary: Moments where gestures or comments dismiss the speaker in front of others.
examples: My manager rolled his eyes when I asked about the budget.
My teenager muttered "whatever" and slammed the bedroom door.
A teammate whispered to another person and laughed after I spoke.

label: When listening feels one-sided
summary: Moments where partners or clients talk over you or insist you never listen.
examples: My partner said I never listen when we talked about chores.
During the call, the client talked over every proposal.
The conversation kept looping because my input was interrupted.

label: Walkouts during presentations
summary: Abandoning the room mid-presentation or slamming notebooks while someone shares.
examples: A coworker slammed her notebook and left during the presentation.
Someone walked out as I showed the final slide.
The room fell silent after the door closed behind them.

label: Missed fouls and officiating gaps
summary: Referees overlooking fouls or making no-calls that impact fairness and safety.
examples: The referee missed three fouls in a row.
No whistle blew when our player was shoved.
The bench kept shouting about the no-call.

label: Fairness in lines and shared resources
summary: When service staff or shoppers bypass the queue or reach over you for the last item.
examples: The barista served someone who arrived after me.
Another shopper reached over my shoulder for the last carton.
I stayed in line but others jumped ahead.

label: Shared space upkeep and boundaries
summary: Living with others who leave messes or return shared items without care.
examples: Dishes piled up again in the sink before work.
A borrowed car came back with an empty tank.
Shared chores keep getting skipped.

label: Employment status surprises
summary: Contract endings or renewals delivered without context or warning.
examples: HR emailed that my contract wasn't renewed without a reason.
A contract ended without anyone explaining why.
Employment status shifted with no warning.

label: Feedback without specifics
summary: Critiques that label work as sloppy or list mistakes without examples.
examples: A teacher wrote 'sloppy' across the assignment.
A review listed mistakes without concrete examples.
Feedback lacked specifics about what to adjust.

label: Maintenance requests with no follow-up
summary: Landlords or contractors who ignore repairs or miss appointments without notice.
examples: Messages about the leak went unanswered.
A contractor missed the appointment and never called.
Maintenance issues linger without updates.

label: Care visits that feel rushed
summary: Providers who glance at the clock or otherwise signal impatience while you explain symptoms.
examples: The doctor kept checking the clock mid-appointment.
A provider glanced at the clock while I spoke.
The visit felt rushed instead of attentive.

label: Workload stacking and late-night pings
summary: Teams that hand you every follow-up task or bosses who ping late at night without regard for rest.
examples: All the follow-up tasks landed on my plate again.
Slack pings came in around midnight from my boss.
I keep getting the action items after every meeting.

label: Disconnected dinners
summary: Shared meals where someone stays on their phone instead of engaging.
examples: Phones stayed on the table during dinner.
Conversation faded while someone scrolled.
I looked up and saw them on their screen instead of with me.

label: Noisy rideshares
summary: Drivers who fill the car with loud speakerphone calls or chatter during the ride.
examples: A driver talked loudly on speakerphone the whole trip.
The car felt like a call center during the ride.
Noise filled the ride instead of quiet.

label: Early-morning noise
summary: Neighbors or surroundings that create loud noise before the day starts.
examples: A dog barked for thirty minutes at 6 a.m.
Weekend mornings start with loud barking next door.
Noise woke me up before sunrise.

label: Traffic safety scares
summary: Cyclists or others rushing through red lights where pedestrians cross.
examples: A cyclist ran the red light through the crosswalk.
Bikes sped through while the walk signal was on.
Someone on a bike ignored the traffic signal next to me.

label: Noticing my own delays
summary: Recognizing when you scroll or stall instead of following through on your plans.
examples: I scrolled instead of returning an important call.
An hour went by on my phone before I reached out.
I delayed following through because I kept scrolling.

label: Teammates catching mistakes before they spread
summary: When coworkers double-check work and spot errors before they reach others.
examples: A teammate double-checked an expense report and caught an error before it went out.
Someone on the team spotted a calculation mistake and flagged it before the client saw it.
A coworker reviewed my draft and found a typo in the headline.

label: Celebrations of personal milestones
summary: Coaches or teammates who visibly celebrate your progress or new personal bests.
examples: At the 8 a.m. session, the trainer high-fived me after I racked 185 pounds on squats.
The coach paused practice to high-five me when the board showed my new record.
Teammates clapped while the trainer called out the weight I just logged.

label: Neighbors lending a hand
summary: Neighbors who step in to clear a path or help with home care while you are away.
examples: A neighbor shoveled our sidewalk while we were gone.
Someone next door cleared the driveway before we got home.
Our neighbor salted the steps so we wouldn't slip.

label: Specific appreciation and thank-yous
summary: Heartfelt notes or emails that name what you contributed and why it mattered.
examples: At 4 p.m., the coordinator emailed naming the volunteer shifts I covered on Saturday.
The principal highlighted the exact stations I staffed during the fundraiser.
A manager DM’d the timestamps where I stepped in during the launch.

label: Reflective listening during support sessions
summary: Counselors or listeners who mirror your words before offering input so you feel heard.
examples: A therapist reflected my words before sharing ideas.
A counselor paused to mirror back what I said.
A support group facilitator summarized my message first.

label: Loved ones and leads sharing the load
summary: Partners or managers who redistribute tasks so responsibilities feel shared.
examples: My partner handled dinner and dishes so I could finish a deadline.
During Monday's sprint review, the project manager assigned two follow-up tasks to each teammate.
A friend swapped shifts so we split the weekend coverage.

label: Strangers returning lost items intact
summary: Moments when someone brings back what you dropped with nothing missing.
examples: Outside the market at 3 p.m., a stranger handed back my wallet with the cash still inside.
Security called me to pick up my phone after a customer turned it in at the front desk.
A passerby jogged over with the keys I dropped on the sidewalk.

label: Quick responses to time-off requests
summary: Leaders who respond promptly when you ask for time away from work.
examples: My manager approved my vacation request the same day.
HR confirmed my PTO within a few hours.
A supervisor okayed my time off without delay.

label: Care teams offering calm, attentive updates
summary: Medical staff who explain steps or check in to reassure you and your loved ones.
examples: A nurse checked in overnight to make sure my dad was comfortable.
A dentist explained each step before starting the procedure.
A tech walked us through the test process in advance.

label: Deliveries marked complete with nothing there
summary: Orders showing as delivered when no package actually arrived.
examples: At 7 p.m. the app marked my dinner order delivered while the porch camera still showed an empty doorstep.
The tracker pinged "delivered" even though the hallway camera never recorded a drop-off.
Courier status flipped to delivered, but the lobby shelf stayed empty all night.

label: Late arrivals without notice
summary: Friends or contacts who show up far past the meeting time without sending a heads-up.
examples: A friend arrived half an hour late with no text.
Someone showed up late to lunch without a heads-up.
My date was 30 minutes late and never messaged.

label: Unexpected policy warning letters
summary: Associations or boards that send a warning without first talking it through.
examples: The HOA sent a lawn warning letter without asking first.
A board left a notice about hedge height with no conversation.
Management posted a warning about patio chairs without talking to us.

label: Credit given to the wrong person
summary: Moments when someone else claims your idea or contribution in front of others.
examples: A colleague took credit for my idea in the pitch.
Someone presented my work as theirs during the meeting.
An editor left my name off the project summary.

label: Care teams that miss critical updates
summary: Childcare or health providers who forget to call about urgent symptoms.
examples: Daycare forgot to call when my child had a fever.
The clinic didn't phone about a concerning result.
Camp missed letting us know about an injury.

label: Transit drivers who wait for you
summary: Drivers who pause the route so you can catch up and ride.
examples: A bus driver waited as I ran toward the stop.
The train conductor held the doors when I called out.
A shuttle driver paused so I could board.

label: Team updates that go missing
summary: Moments when teammates skip shared boards or updates for days at a time.
examples: From Monday through Friday, no cards under Jordan's initials moved on the shared sprint board.
The kanban view shows five tasks assigned to Sam untouched since last Tuesday.
Our tracker still lists Casey's items in "In Progress" after a full week.

label: Repairs handled right away
summary: Landlords or maintenance crews who respond quickly to repair requests.
examples: Maintenance fixed the leak the day after we reported it.
Our landlord scheduled a plumber the next morning.
The repair team showed up within 24 hours.

label: When repayment promises slip
summary: Friends or relatives who miss the payback they said was coming soon.
examples: A sibling missed the repayment they promised Friday.
A friend still hasn't paid me back after saying they would.
Someone delayed sending the money again.

label: Allergy instructions ignored
summary: Restaurants that serve allergens even after you clearly note them.
examples: The restaurant served my meal with peanuts after I flagged my allergy.
Catering included dairy even though I mentioned the allergy.
A cafe added walnuts despite my warning.

label: Meetings scheduled over breaks
summary: Managers who drop meetings onto your lunch or rest time without asking.
examples: My manager scheduled a meeting over my lunch break without asking.
A lead booked a call during my only break.
Someone added a meeting right over my dinner time.

label: Support staff who follow up
summary: Helpers who guide you through a fix and check back afterward.
examples: Yesterday the service agent stayed on the call for each troubleshooting step and emailed this morning to confirm the fix.
IT kept the remote session open until the app loaded and sent a ticket update at 9 a.m.
Customer service called back the next day after guiding me through the reset.

label: City fixes after persistent outreach
summary: Public works teams that finally resolve an issue after repeated contact.
examples: The city fixed the streetlight after months of emails.
Public works repaired the pothole we kept reporting.
The utilities crew finally addressed the outage after persistent follow-up.

label: Digital communication gaps
summary: Messages acknowledged but unanswered in digital channels.
examples: A friend saw my urgent text and left me on read for two days.
My manager replied with only a thumbs-up emoji to my detailed update.
The family group chat stayed silent when I asked for help with a prescription.

label: Identity and pronoun disrespect
summary: Misgendering, deadnaming, and cultural disrespect that erase identity.
examples: A nurse kept calling me sir after I shared my pronouns.
A teacher read my child's old name at the ceremony.
A coworker mocked my accent in front of clients.

label: Accessibility and accommodation gaps
summary: Requests for access features ignored or refused, leaving people without support.
examples: The venue had steps and no ramp so my wheelchair could not enter.
The company livestream started without the captions we requested.
Management refused to move the daily check-in later after I requested an accommodation for chronic pain.

label: Healthcare and affirming care barriers
summary: Care teams dismiss symptoms, deny medication, or block affirming support.
examples: The specialist said to just relax after another failed IVF cycle.
The urgent clinic doctor ended the visit without explaining warning signs after my miscarriage.
Insurance marked the pre-authorization for my gender-affirming surgery consult as denied with no appeal contact.

label: Civic and bureaucratic obstacles
summary: Institutional processes that detain, delay, or deny without clear recourse.
examples: Border agents separated our family for secondary screening without explanation.
Police searched me during my commute while waving others through.
The benefits office lost my paperwork and made me restart the process.

label: Environmental safety disruptions
summary: Climate and infrastructure emergencies that leave people without safe options.
examples: Wildfire smoke closed the school and the district site listed no backup plan.
A flash flood washed out the only road out of town overnight.
Utility alerts gave only minutes of warning before a rolling blackout.
